decisions.reason: As a multi-model line on its own webpage that directly extends the established geospatial stack, it embodies visible sunk investment and strategic continuity, so management is likely to keep backing it and read any weak signals as normal adoption lag.

The building data digital twin service supports the firm's announced move toward integrated and emerging geospatial solutions, so despite only moderate visibility management would likely continue and explain any shortfall by an immature market rather than by a flawed commitment.

This identity-related service is the most exposed after the earlier withdrawal of Product E, but because it still complements enterprise integration needs and already carries development responsibility, management is more likely to persist than to exit immediately.

An open GIS application development framework is highly consistent with the firm's open, extensible and user-centered positioning, and as a product line it likely involved enough effort and reputational commitment to discourage withdrawal.

The consulting workshop sits squarely in the firm's core consulting and training business and was given its own page at launch, so management would usually allow more time for market build-up before removing it.
